introduction: VA offers several benefit programs for eligible veterans and, in some cases, dependents or survivors. Choose the benefit you need rather than treating VA benefits as one application.

who: Eligibility varies by benefit and can depend on service history, disability, family relationship and other program rules. Accredited assistance can help identify the appropriate claim.
sections.get: Benefits include disability compensation, education and training, and housing-related assistance. Each program has its own decision and application pathway.
sections.docs: Prepare service records and documents relevant to the requested benefit. For education, VA lists identity, banking, military or education history and school information. Ask about a dependent or survivor application when the benefit is based on another person’s service.
sections.apply: Use VA’s benefit application directory. It links to disability, pension, education and other programs and explains alternatives to online filing. Ask a VA accredited representative for claim assistance if needed.
sections.after: Track each claim and respond to requests from the relevant VA program. Read the decision before choosing any review or appeal route. Keep separate records for separate benefits.
sections.sources:
• VA benefit application directory
  • VA education applications

  • USA Assistance background and screenshots

faqs: Is one application enough for every VA benefit?
No. Use the application for the particular benefit.
Some programs cover dependents or survivors under their own requirements.
Does housing assistance mean a free home?
VA housing programs include loans and adaptation assistance; the specific program determines eligibility and terms.
Can someone help with the claim?
VA encourages assistance from accredited representatives.

provenance.review_scope: Program purpose, eligibility pathway and application methods; no unverified dollar limits published.
